rationale: ⲡⲱϣⲙ 'breath, exhalation' + ⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'fragrance.' Compound for the soul's/spirit's fragrant breathing-forth — given to Adam alongside hope at his awakening. Manichaean cosmological-anthropological term.

Greek ἀναίρεσις 'destruction, removal, taking-away.' Two scribal variants on the same page (lines 15, 19). Technical eschatological term for the cosmic dissolution at the end — paired with ⲡⲟⲩⲱⲑ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ at line 23.
ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄/ⲟⲩⲱⲑ + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'pass over forth' = 'wipe out, dissolve.' Eschatological pair-partner with ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄ 'formation' at line 23-24 — the cosmic dissolution-with-reformation at the End.
From ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄ 'shape, fashion, form.' Cosmological term for the constructed/shaped order. At line 24 paired with ⲟⲩⲱⲑ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ as the eschatological dyad: dissolution+reformation.
Lyc reflex of ⲕⲱⲛⲥ̄ 'wrap, embrace, surround.' Used at line 15 of the First Man encompassing the totality at the final destruction.
Reduplicated form of ϩⲱϣⲙ̄ 'afflict.' Used in the punitive triplet 'expel / bind / afflict' (line 1).
Greek πέσσειν 'cook, ripen, digest.' Used in the hot-stone-in-milk simile at line 31. Standard Greek loanword for thermal-chemical transformation of food.

Etymology unclear. Context (line 26) requires a small heated object that a man takes and plunges into milk to cook it. Possibly related to ⲱⲃϣ̄ 'white(-hot)' or ⲱⲃⲣ 'iron.' Fits ancient cooking technique of dropping hot stones/irons into liquid. Flag for parallels.
Lyc spelling of ⲣⲱⲕϩ 'burn.' Distinguished from ⲣⲱⲭⲍ̄ in glossary — both reflect ⲣⲱⲕϩ but in different registers.
